state:
Goal `core-session`, stage 2. `Core\Session::clear`, `destroy`, `get`, `remove` and `set` have all their feature proofs: about, three examples, an attack, a bench with a recorded figure, a Rust `covers:` test and a card in the plain voice. `Core\Session` has a class card. Four members still owe examples, hostile, perf and a Rust `covers:` test: `start`, `regenerate`, `setSecret`, `getSecret`.

Every Session proof needs a real store and a real request. The shape is on disk under `docs/examples/core/Session/remove/`: an `nvs.toml` in the feature directory that grants `[capabilities.cache] shared`, sets `[session] backend = "shared"` and `[cache.shared] url = "redis://127.0.0.1:16379"`, and a `.nvsr` beside each program. `tests/hostile/core/Session/<member>/` has the same pair. `benches/members/core/Session/nvs.toml` already serves every Session bench, so a new bench needs only its own `.nvs` and `.nvsr`. Redis is `tests/db/compose.yaml`'s service, which the goal's `env.docker` brings up.

`set`, `get`, `remove` and `clear` never reach the store: they change the request's copy, and the write happens once at the end. Their Rust tests open a session with `ctx.open_session(nvs_runtime::Session { .. write_back: super::send_at_end })` and call the member through `nvs_runtime::call`, as `set_saves_a_value_replaces_it_and_earns_a_write` does. A member that does talk to the store (`start`, `regenerate`, `destroy`) is tested the way `destroy_forgets_the_record_before_it_closes_the_session` does it: `crate::tests::granting` with a `[cache.shared] url` pointing at the loopback `serving` fake. Such a member costs a round trip per call (about 0.7 ms), so its bench uses a few thousand iterations.

A bench's figure goes stale whenever `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/session.rs` changes. After the last Rust edit, run `bun nv proofs --verify --id '<member>'` for each member you touched (the `--group` run hides a failing attack while other members owe), and `--record-perf --id '<member>'` for each it names stale.

items.text: **`Core\Session::setSecret` and `getSecret`** — owe examples, hostile, perf, tests (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`). The cards are `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/session.rs:467` and `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/session.rs:512`, the members `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/session.rs:1192` and `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/session.rs:1224`. Rewrite both cards in the plain voice, as `SET_DOC` now is. Neither reaches the store, so the Rust test has the shape of `set_saves_a_value_replaces_it_and_earns_a_write`, which follows `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/session.rs:1993`.

**`Core\Session::regenerate`** — owes the same. The card is `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/session.rs:421`, the member `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/session.rs:1309`. It issues a new identifier through the store, so its Rust test uses the loopback `serving` fake and its bench a few thousand iterations.

**`Core\Session::start`** — owes the same. The card is `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/session.rs:278`, the member `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/session.rs:775`. Starting twice in one request is the edge an attack reaches for.
